=== callisto.toml ===
# callisto configuration
#
# Mirrors ~/projects/michi's proven callisto.toml shape — the closest
# existing reference for a Rust-crates + NAPI-binding + npm-wrapper
# monorepo. One structural difference from michi: michi's NAPI crate and
# its npm wrapper share a single directory (packages/michi-node/, holding
# both Cargo.toml and package.json), whereas this repo splits them across
# crates/binding (the cdylib) and packages/napi (the npm wrapper) — expressed
# as two separate [[package]] entries joined by a [[fixed-group]] below, the
# same mechanism michi uses for its own crate+wrapper pair.
#
# `[[package]] match` is a PACKAGE NAME (bare, or "<ecosystem>/<name>"
# ecosystem-qualified — one of cargo/npm/pypi/go/maven/nuget/deno/jsr),
# never a directory path — confirmed against callisto-model's PackageId::parse
# and callisto-graph's own test suite (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/
# resolve.rs, tests/per_package_config_test.rs). A directory-path `match`
# (e.g. "crates/core") parses to a literal bare name that no real package is
# ever named, so the rule silently matches nothing — verified empirically:
# an earlier draft of this file used directory paths for every [[package]]
# entry and callisto plan-publish still listed crates/binding for a cratesIo
# publish despite publish-to = [] below, because that override was never
# actually being applied. michi's own callisto.toml has this same mistake
# (match = "packages/michi-node", match = "."), which is presumably why it
# went unnoticed there too — its manifest-derived defaults happen to already
# match what it wants.
#
# NOT YET ACTIVATED. .github/workflows/release.yml runs the real
# callisto-action (mirroring ~/projects/michi's setup) but is deliberately
# left unpinned to `latest`/`main` until callisto's own repo cuts a GitHub
# Release past v0.3.0 — its git tags/crates.io have moved on to 0.3.3
# already (confirmed via `cargo install callisto-cli`, which pulled 0.3.3
# straight from crates.io) without a corresponding GitHub Release being cut,
# and setup-callisto's binary-download fallback path depends on that Release
# existing.
#
# No .moon/workspace.yml changes were needed: despite callisto's README
# documenting a moon WASM-extension install step
# (extensions.callisto.plugin = ".../callisto-moon.wasm"), michi — the only
# real working reference — has no `extensions:` block at all, and the
# extension (crates/callisto-moon) only implements read-only `status`/
# `plan-publish` reporting subcommands — no `publish`/`tag`/apply path exists
# through it, and its own gix-based git-read spike is explicitly "never
# enabled in the shipped wasm". callisto-action installs its own `callisto`
# CLI binary directly onto $GITHUB_PATH via setup-callisto instead; moon is
# installed alongside it as a toolchain dependency, not as callisto's host.

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

# Rust library crate — published to crates.io, no npm counterpart. Consumed
# via path dependency by both crates/cli and crates/binding.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-core"
publish-to = ["cratesIo"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Rust CLI crate — published to crates.io. packages/cli wraps its compiled
# per-platform binaries for npm distribution; kept in lockstep below.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen"
publish-to = ["cratesIo"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# npm CLI wrapper — distributes crates/cli's compiled binaries.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/cli"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# NAPI binding crate (cdylib) — not published to crates.io independently (no
# real-world use case for `cargo add`ing an FFI shim on its own). Callisto
# still tracks/bumps its version to stay in lockstep with its npm wrapper via
# the fixed-group below, but is excluded from the crates.io publish plan.
#
# publish-to = [] alone is NOT sufficient — verified against the real
# callisto 0.3.3 binary that a Cargo.toml with no explicit `publish` field
# still gets treated as publishable by callisto-manifests' own
# is_publishable() default (missing key = true), independent of this
# override. crates/binding/Cargo.toml's own `publish = false` is the actual
# gate; this declaration documents the intent and is kept for when/if
# publish-to ever becomes independently authoritative.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-napi"
publish-to = []
release-trigger = "changeset"

# npm NAPI wrapper — distributes crates/binding's compiled .node binaries.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Vite plugin — standalone npm package, no Rust counterpart.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Keep the NAPI binding crate and its npm wrapper versioned in lockstep —
# the npm package is meaningless without a matching binding build.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "napi-and-binding"
members = ["oxc-react-docgen-napi", "@oxc-react-docgen/napi"]

# Keep the CLI crate and its npm wrapper versioned in lockstep — the npm
# package just redistributes this crate's compiled binaries.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "cli-and-npm-wrapper"
members = ["oxc-react-docgen", "@oxc-react-docgen/cli"]

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged managed release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@c3ec0de9ae7f1019cea21aa96aa0a895b9552063 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@c3ec0de9ae7f1019cea21aa96aa0a895b9552063 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@c3ec0de9ae7f1019cea21aa96aa0a895b9552063 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Verify workflow contracts and reject mutable action references
        run: just workflow-contracts

  recovery-checks:
    name: Check release workflow policy for recovery
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_source_sha != ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install ripgrep
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@c3ec0de9ae7f1019cea21aa96aa0a895b9552063 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Verify release workflow contracts
        run: just release-workflow-checks

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, recovery-checks]
    # Exactly one gate runs per event; a failed gate matches neither clause.
    if: >-
      always() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      ((needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.recovery-checks.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.recovery-checks.result == 'success' && needs.verify.result == 'skipped'))
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Attestations are stamped with this run's own SHA, so the
          # coordinator must be exactly the revision running this workflow.
          orchestration_sha="$TRIGGERING_SHA"
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
              echo "orchestration_sha=$orchestration_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # This workspace bumps interdependent Cargo packages together, so a
          # bumped member's own Cargo.lock entry goes stale without this --
          # see ARCHITECTURE.md's "Lockfile Staleness" section.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.slots.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The coordinator must be the current workflow revision. Recovery
          # never rebuilds its release engine from historic source.
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --profile production --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          shasum -a 256 "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json" > "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json.sha256"
      - name: Read declared artifact slot count
        id: slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "has_artifacts=$(jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build-artifact:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} from the intent-bound source tree
    needs: [plan, release-candidate]
    if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
          - id: wasm-wasi
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: wasm32-wasip1
            asset: callisto-moon.wasm
            kind: wasm
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify handoff
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts"
      - name: Build declared artifact
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/release-source
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh
      - name: Attest exact artifact bytes
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Assemble attested product artifacts
    needs: [build-artifact, release-candidate, plan]
    if: always() && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' && needs.build-artifact.result == 'success'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      orchestration_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-macos-arm64
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-linux-gnu
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-linux-musl
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-wasm-wasi
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - name: Create exact artifact manifest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts" --out "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts/manifest.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]
    # Artifact-less sources skip build; a failed or cancelled build must still block.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'false' || needs.build.result == 'success')
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The release-source checkout alone needs Git credentials because
          # graph-owned tag dispatch pushes from this repository.
          persist-credentials: true
      # Downloaded outside the workspace (under $RUNNER_TEMP, like
      # setup-callisto's own binary install): callisto release execute
      # re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which requires a
      # worktree with no tracked or untracked files -- landing these inside
      # the checkout would dirty it and fail that check before anything
      # gets published.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        env:
          HAS_ARTIFACTS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          (cd "$intent_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          if [[ "$HAS_ARTIFACTS" == true ]]; then
            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          fi
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json" --receipt "$state_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --profile production)
          if [[ -n "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT" ]]; then
            args+=(--recovery)
          fi
          if [[ -f "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$build_dir/release-artifacts")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload receipt and execution state
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-receipt
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-state/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

> [!TIP]
> Run `callisto version --dry-run` locally anytime to inspect calculated version bumps and changelog updates with colored diffs before committing.

---

## Publishing Packages

`callisto version` bumps and commits; publishing to a registry is a separate, explicit step, split into commands that each do one thing and pass JSON to the next:

```bash
# 1. Compute what's ready to publish (read-only, no network)
callisto plan-publish --format json > plan.json

# 2. Publish each package to its registry (cargo/npm/twine), independently —
#    one package's rejection doesn't block the others
callisto publish --format json > report.json

# 3. Narrow the plan down to what the report confirms actually succeeded —
#    so one package's failure doesn't cost its already-shipped siblings a tag
callisto filter-plan --plan plan.json --report report.json > shipped.json

# 4. Tag the commits that shipped, moving any floating major alias (e.g. v1)
callisto tag --plan shipped.json --floating-major
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant CI as CI / callisto-action
  participant CLI as callisto CLI
  participant Reg as Registries
  participant Git as git remote

  CI->>CLI: plan-publish --format json
  CLI-->>CI: PublishPlan
  CI->>CLI: publish --format json
  CLI->>Reg: publish per package (cargo / npm / twine)
  Reg-->>CLI: per-package outcome
  CLI-->>CI: PublishReport
  CI->>CLI: filter-plan --plan --report
  CLI-->>CI: plan narrowed to confirmed successes
  CI->>CLI: tag --plan --floating-major
  CLI->>Git: create tags, move floating alias
```

`callisto-action` (the bundled GitHub Action) now creates or updates only the version PR. The repository release workflow performs plan/build/attested execute after that PR merges; see [`docs/06-publishing.md`](docs/06-publishing.md).

---

## Release Workflow & Branch Configuration

Callisto integrates natively with GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and custom release pipelines.

### 1. Release PR Branch Naming & Configuration

When Callisto generates automated release pull requests, it targets the default release branch **`changeset-release/main`** (matching `@changesets/action` standards).

You can override the release branch name per invocation using the `--branch` flag:

```bash
# Generate PR body targeting a custom release branch
callisto compose-pr-body --branch release-packages
```

### 2. Production GitHub Actions Workflow (`release.yml`)

Create `.github/workflows/release.yml` to automate version bumps and registry publishing on `push` to `main`:

```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release / Version Packages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write  # OIDC registry publishing

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install Rust Toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Run Callisto Release Action
        uses: orin-dx/callisto-action@v1
        with:
          branch: changeset-release/main
          # The release workflow performs publication after merge.
```

### 3. Bypassing Heavy CI Workflows on Release PRs

Release PRs contain automated version bumps and changelog updates. To prevent running expensive CI build matrices on release PRs, ignore `changeset-release/**` branches in your main `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches-ignore:
      - 'changeset-release/**'
```

# Publishing with Callisto

This document covers authentication setup for registry publishing, with particular attention
to npm, where there are two distinct auth patterns and common points of confusion.

---

## Repository durable-release workflow

Callisto's own `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` separates release work into four
authority boundaries. A push with pending changesets creates or updates the release PR. That
PR versions manifests and changelogs and removes only the changesets it consumed. Nothing is
removed from `main` until that PR is merged.

The normal GitHub flow keeps one `callisto/version-packages` release PR and recomputes it from
the current base branch whenever changesets land. This is a reconstruction from `main`, not a
literal rebase of an old generated commit: recomputation prevents stale version, changelog, or
changeset-deletion edits from being carried forward. The action never runs a local `git push`
to update that branch. Instead it stages the recomputed change as a commit rooted at the
current `main` via GitHub's `createCommitOnBranch` commit API, restricted to non-workflow
paths so `.github/workflows/*` is always inherited unchanged from the branch's current tip,
then moves the release branch's ref onto that commit with a plain REST ref update. GitHub's
built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/*` through the Git push protocol or
through `createCommitOnBranch`'s own file changes on a public repository, but a ref move that
carries no workflow-file write is not subject to that restriction, so the built-in token never
needs elevated permission to keep the branch current. The resulting commits are GitHub-signed
("Verified") and attributed to `github-actions[bot]`. Repositories that already have a
SHA-suffixed branch and PR from before this change (created under the prior fallback behavior)
do not need to migrate anything -- that branch is a normal, continuously-updated managed branch
going forward. An optional App or fine-grained token remains available for repositories that
want release PR operations attributed to a different identity, but is never required.

After a merge, the workflow derives a transient release intent from the signed merge commit's
actual delta, builds from that exact commit, and passes the intent between jobs as a same-run
GitHub artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar. It is not committed and it is never recovered from a
cache. The execute job rechecks the handoff before calling `callisto release execute`.

Create a GitHub Environment named `release` before enabling registry credentials. Configure
at least one required reviewer and appropriate branch/tag deployment rules in the repository's
Environment settings. The workflow queries the Environment API and fails if the reviewer rule
is absent; the `environment: release` job boundary is what prevents registry secrets from being
available to planning or build jobs.

An administrator must also enable a branch-protection rule or ruleset on `main` that requires
CODEOWNERS review. [`.github/CODEOWNERS`](../.github/CODEOWNERS) names the real owner for
workflow and action changes, but GitHub does not enforce review merely because that file exists.

Only the `execute` job may receive `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, or `TWINE_PASSWORD`.
Do not put those secrets at workflow scope, in build jobs, or in an action input. Binary releases
add exact files plus `release-artifacts/manifest.json` to the build handoff; their GitHub build
attestations are verified by Callisto before upload. Source-only releases do not need that
manifest.

`callisto-action` is now a compatibility version-PR action only. Its former `publish` and
`create_github_release` inputs are ignored; it never publishes, tags, downloads artifacts, or
creates a forge release. The repository durable workflow is the supported release path.

---

## npm Registry Authentication

Callisto delegates all npm publishing to the `npm` or `pnpm` CLI (see the coordinator
pattern in `00-design.md` §11.1 and §9). This means callisto never reads NPM credentials
directly — whatever auth the npm CLI can see when it runs is what gets used. There are two
supported patterns.

---

### Pattern A: Manual `.npmrc` setup via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret in your repository. Add this only in the protected `execute`
job, immediately before the command that publishes:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent .release-intent/release-intent.json
```

This works because `npm config set` writes to the user-level `.npmrc`, which the npm CLI
reads for every subsequent publish call in the same job.

The version-PR action never receives this token. It only creates or updates a reviewed PR.

---

### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`

`actions/setup-node` has built-in npm auth support: when you pass `registry-url`, it writes
a project-level `.npmrc` configured to read the token from the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` environment
variable. Set `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in the job environment:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'
    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

- run: callisto release execute --intent .release-intent/release-intent.json
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

**How this works:** `actions/setup-node` writes an `.npmrc` file containing a line like:
`//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. The npm CLI evaluates this shell
expansion at publish time, picking up the environment variable. Without the `.npmrc` entry
written by `setup-node`, setting `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` alone has no effect — npm does not read
that variable unless a corresponding `.npmrc` line tells it to.

**Warning:** `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` is silently ignored by npm if no `.npmrc` contains a
`${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` interpolation. If you set `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in your workflow but did
not also run `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` set, your publish will fail with an
authentication error — not a variable-not-found error, because npm never reads the variable
in that case.

---

### Choosing a pattern

| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
|---|---|---|
| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
| Recommended when | Your execute job does not otherwise need Node setup | Your execute job already uses `setup-node` |
| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |

If your execute job already calls `actions/setup-node` and sets `registry-url`, Pattern B
works because `setup-node` wrote the `.npmrc`. Do not add `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` to a job that
does not run `setup-node` with `registry-url`.

---

## npm Platform/Main Package Publishing

A napi-rs (or maturin) native package publishes as **N platform-specific packages** — one
per target triple, e.g. `my-lib-linux-x64-gnu`, `my-lib-darwin-arm64` — plus **one main
package** that end users actually install. The main package's `optionalDependencies` pin
exact versions of every platform sibling; npm resolves whichever one matches the installer's
OS/arch at install time. See `00-design.md` §5.3 and §7.5 for how platform packages are
detected from `napi.targets`/`[tool.maturin].targets`.

### Publish order

`callisto publish` publishes in this fixed order: Rust crates → npm platform packages → npm
main packages → PyPI packages. Platform packages always publish before the main package that
depends on them.

### What happens when a platform package fails

If a platform package fails to publish in the same run, its dependent main package is
**skipped, not attempted** — publishing it anyway would ship `optionalDependencies` pointing
at a version that was never uploaded. The skipped entry appears in the publish report as:

```json
{
  "package": "npm/my-lib",
  "status": "failed",
  "errorKind": "dependencyFailed",
  "error": "skipped: platform dependency failed to publish: my-lib-linux-x64-gnu"
}
```

`dependencyFailed` means exactly this — the main package was never attempted, because a
declared platform dependency failed to publish *in this same run*. It is not itself a
registry error. **Remediation:** fix whatever made the platform package fail, then re-run
`callisto publish` — it is idempotent and will skip anything already uploaded.

### What happens when a platform dependency is missing entirely

Before any registry call is made, `callisto plan-publish` cross-checks every main package's
declared platform dependencies against what actually ended up in the plan. A dependency is
allowed to be absent only if it's already published (its on-disk version already matches its
last release tag). Otherwise — a misconfigured platform package with no npm publish target,
or one excluded via `--package` — planning fails outright with a `MissingPlatformDependency`
error naming the main package and the missing dependency, before anything is published.

## Cargo (crates.io) Authentication

Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment.
`cargo publish` reads it directly:

```yaml
env:
  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
```

No `.cargo/credentials` setup step is needed; cargo recognizes the environment variable
natively.

---

## Python (PyPI) Authentication

Python publishing uses `twine upload`. Twine reads credentials from two environment
variables: `TWINE_USERNAME` (set to `__token__` when using a PyPI API token) and
`TWINE_PASSWORD` (set to the API token value). Set these in the job environment before
the Callisto release action runs:

```yaml
env:
  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
```

Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognise that variable name.

## Full workflow example with npm auth (Pattern A)

This extends the Paradigm 1 example from `release-paradigms.md` to include npm publishing:

```yaml
name: Release & Publish Workflow

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify CI Pipeline
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
      - run: moon run :format-check
      - run: moon run :lint
      - run: moon run :test

  release:
    name: Version Packages or Publish Release
    needs: [verify]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
      - uses: ./.github/actions/callisto-action
        # This action only creates or updates the release PR. Registry tokens
        # belong exclusively in the protected execute job after merge.
```

        CRATE_VERSION="${TAG_NAME#callisto@}"; CRATE_VERSION="${CRATE_VERSION#callisto-cli@}"

        # Pick a download destination whose extension matches ASSET_NAME
        # (under $RUNNER_TEMP, never the workspace) so the extraction step
        # below always has an archive it can actually open -- a hardcoded
        # ".tar.gz" path here previously masked the fact that Windows assets
        # are zip files, since tar -xzf can't read a zip regardless of what
        # the file on disk is really named.
        case "$ASSET_NAME" in
          *.zip)
            DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.zip"
            ;;
          *.tar.gz)
            DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
            ;;
          *)
            DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
            ;;

        # GitHub attestation from the Callisto release workflow before it is
        # extracted. require aborts on failure; fallback discards the asset and
        # returns 1 so the crates.io path runs; skip trusts the asset.
        verify_asset() {
          local reason=""
          if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "skip" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::verification=skip: $ASSET_NAME was not verified"
            return 0
          fi
          if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            reason="gh is not installed"
          elif ! gh attestation verify "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" \

            echo "::error::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason (verification=require)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
# content digest.
set -euo pipefail

status=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  reference=${line#*uses: }
  reference=${reference%% #*}
  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue
  if [[ "$reference" == docker://* ]]; then
    valid='^docker://[^@[:space:]]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'
  else
    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'
  fi
  if [[ ! "$reference" =~ $valid ]]; then
    printf 'mutable or malformed external action reference: %s\n' "$line" >&2
    status=1
  fi
done < <(rg --no-heading --glob '*.yml' --glob '*.yaml' '^\s*uses:\s*' .github)
codeowners=.github/CODEOWNERS
if [[ ! -f "$codeowners" ]] \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/workflows/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners" \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/actions/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners"; then
  printf 'CODEOWNERS must cover .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ with a real owner\n' >&2
  status=1
fi
exit "$status"

name: Release & Publish

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

        description: 'Merged Callisto release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'

# and registry credentials exist only inside the `execute` job.
permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  # Callisto 0.8 split releasing into two authority boundaries: the action only
  # creates or updates the release PR, and publication happens from the merged
  # release commit under the repository's own durable workflow (this file).
  # `publish: true` no longer exists as an action input -- see
  # https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/main/docs/06-publishing.md.
  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1

          # parent-to-merge delta against the committed decision file; PR

      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

        env:

            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \

            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"

    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [release-candidate, plan]

      group: release-execute

      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256

      # user-level .npmrc for every publish in this job. pnpm (this repo's
      # package manager, which callisto shells out to) honours the same file.
      - name: Authenticate with the npm registry
        env:

          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source"
            --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json"
            --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json"
            --receipt "$state_dir/release-receipt.json"
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
            --profile production
          )
          if [[ -n "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT" ]]; then
            args+=(--recovery)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'

              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: release-receipt
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-state/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

content.text:
Repo now tracks callisto 0.8. Four changes:

**`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — rewritten. 0.8 removed the action's `publish` input: `callisto-action` only creates/updates the release PR, and publication is the repo's own job. New shape: `release-candidate` (identify a merged, GitHub-verified `callisto/version-packages` merge) → `version-pr` *or* `plan` (`callisto release plan --from-release-commit --decision .callisto/release-decision.json`) → `execute` (`callisto release execute`, tokens only in that job, `environment: release`). Intent passes between jobs as a same-run artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar. Added `workflow_dispatch` recovery via `release_source_sha`.

Both callisto actions pinned to `c5578e6a` (`callisto@0.8.0`) instead of `@main`, and `setup-callisto` is invoked explicitly with `setup_callisto: 'false'` — that avoids depending on the action's internal `$/.github/actions/...` self-reference resolving for an external consumer, and pins the CLI version here with `verification: require` (0.8.0's assets are attested).

**`callisto.toml`** — `publish-to = ["cratesIo"]` was invalid; the parser accepts `crates-io`. The whole config failed to load, so *none* of the per-package overrides were ever applied. Fixed in both entries. Also qualified `[[fixed-group]]` members (`cargo/oxc-react-docgen`, `npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi`, …) and rewrote the stale header comments. Under 0.8's release path `publish-to = []` on `oxc-react-docgen-napi` *is* authoritative — intent derivation builds publish operations straight from it — so that comment's old caveat no longer applies.

**`package.json`** — the private root package was named `oxc-react-docgen`, colliding with the CLI crate and making every `oxc-react-docgen: patch` changeset ambiguous across cargo/npm. Renamed to `oxc-react-docgen-workspace`; referenced nowhere else, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` keys importers by path. `callisto validate` now passes.

I deliberately did **not** add a `[release]` section: 0.8's `artifact-targets` are validated against callisto's own hardcoded asset-name table, so no other workspace can use it. The plan job asserts the derived intent has zero artifact slots.

Three gaps left open:
- No `release` environment exists on the repo. GitHub will auto-create it unprotected on first use — create it with a required reviewer first.
- Nothing in the release path builds the napi `.node` binaries or CLI binaries, so `@oxc-react-docgen/napi` and `/cli` would publish without their native artifacts. Pre-existing, not a 0.8 regression.
- `execute` isn't gated on CI passing (callisto's own workflow has a `verify` job). Also pre-existing.

Fixing the callisto issue, can you address everything else we need? Any rust updates, crate updates, moon, just, etc? Actions we need to update? Do we need to setup dependabot? Check the callisto repo for inspiration

result.output:
## 2.0.2

#### 🚀 Updates

- Temporarily disabled shallow checkouts triggering a hard error in CI until we can implement a
  better solution. This means that if you have a shallow checkout, you may see incorrect affected
  results, or Git commands may fail.
- Added more logs to `moon docker prune` to help debug edge cases.
- Added `MOON_INCLUDE_RELATIONS` environment variable support for the `--include-relations` CLI
  option.
- Added `.env` and `.env.*` as defaults to the `hasher.ignoreMissingPatterns` setting.

#### 🐞 Fixes

- Fixed an issue where the graph visualizers would not render correctly in the VS Code extension.
- Fixed an issue where a task with `shell: false` would be force enabled when a glob/env was
  detected. We now respect the configured value.
- Fixed an issue where "run" type based tasks would not run in CI.

## 2.0.1

#### 🚀 Updates

- Updated `moon upgrade` to upgrade via proto if we detect that moon is managed by proto. This will
  run `proto install moon latest`.

#### 🐞 Fixes

- Fixed some WASM serialization errors.
- Fixed the `moon upgrade` command not handling the new v2 distribution format correctly. If you are
  on moon v2.0.0, the upgrade command will still be broken until you upgrade to this patch.

## 2.0.0

#### 💥 Breaking

View the [migration guide](https://moonrepo.dev/docs/migrate/2.0) for a full list of breaking
changes and how to easily migrate!

- Renamed "touched files" to "changed files".

- **CLI**
  - Removed canary and nightly releases.
  - Removed commands: `moon node`, `moon migrate from-package-json`, `moon query hash`,
    `moon query hash-diff`
  - Renamed all options and flags to kebab-case instead of camelCase.
  - Reworked many commands and their arguments. Refer to the migration guide for details.
  - Reworked console output handling. Updated `--summary` with different levels.
  - Reworked release distribution to use archives instead of direct executables.
- **Configuration**
  - Renamed, removed, or changed _many_ settings. Refer to the migration guide for details.
  - Renamed `.moon/toolchain.yml` to `.moon/toolchains.yml` (plural).
- **MCP**
  - Updated protocol version to 2025-11-25.
  - Updated `get_projects` and `get_tasks` to return fragments, to reduce the payload size.
- **Projects**
  - Reworked how the `language` is detected.
  - Flattened `project` metadata structure.
- **Tasks**
  - Task inheritance now deep merges instead of shallow merges when dealing with extends and
    multi-global.
  - Task `command` and `args` only support simple commands now. Use `script` for compound commands
    (pipes, redirects, multiple commands, etc).
  - Removed "watcher" task `preset`.
  - Reworked env var merge order, substitution, and more. Refer to the migration guide for details.
  - Reworked `.env` handling.
    - Moved loading to occur before task execution, instead of creation.
    - Can _no longer_ reference task `env` vars for substitution.
- **Toolchain**
  - Removed the old platform system, and replaced it with the new WASM plugin system.
    - All old "stable" toolchains have been replaced with the new "unstable" toolchains.
- **VCS**
  - Reworked the hooks layer for better interoperability.
- **WASM API**
  - Removed the `/cwd` virtual path.
  - Renamed `ProjectFragment.alias` to `ProjectFragment.aliases` and changed its type from
    `Option<String>` to `Vec<String>`.
  - Removed `RegisterExtensionOutput.config_schema` field. Use the new `define_extension_config`
    plugin function instead.

#### 🚀 Updates

View the [announcement blog post](https://moonrepo.dev/blog/moon-v2.0) for all updates, new
features, improvements, and much more!

- **Action pipeline**
  - Will now always generate a hash for a task, even if caching is disabled.
  - Applies "transitive reduction" to the graph, removing unnecessary edges for better performance.
  - Improved console output, logging, and error handling.
  - Improved parallelism when running tasks.
    - Now resolves and expands targets _before_ partitioning.
    - Now partitions _after_ filtering based on affected state.
- **CLI**
  - New commands: `moon exec`, `moon extension`, `moon hash`, `moon projects`, `moon tasks`,
    `moon query affected`, `moon template`
  - Updated commands `moon check`, `moon ci`, and `moon run`:
    - Now uses `moon exec` under the hood.
    - Added levels to `--summary`.
  - Updated commands that require an identifier to prompt for it if not provided.
  - Stabilized the `moonx` binary (which uses `moon exec` under the hood).

import json,urllib.request,re
txt=open("Cargo.toml").read()
sec=txt.split("[workspace.dependencies]",1)[1].split("\n[profile",1)[0]
deps=[]
for line in sec.splitlines():
    line=line.strip()
    if not line or line.startswith("#"): continue
    m=re.match(r'^([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)\s*=\s*(.+)$', line)
    if not m: continue
    name, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    vm=re.search(r'version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', rest) or re.match(r'^"([^"]+)"', rest)
    deps.append((name, vm.group(1) if vm else "?"))
for n,c in deps:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{n}",timeout=20) as r:
            l=json.load(r)["crate"]["max_stable_version"]
    except Exception as e:
        l=f"ERR"
    def parts(s):
        m=re.match(r"(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?",s); return (m.group(1), m.group(2) or "0") if m else ("","")
    cm,lm=parts(c),parts(l)
    flag=""
    if l!="ERR":
        if cm[0]!=lm[0]: flag="   <== MAJOR"
        elif cm[1]!=lm[1]: flag="   <- minor"
    print(f"{n:20} {c:10} -> {l}{flag}")

cat > .github/dependabot.yml <<'YAML'
# Dependency updates. Every ecosystem is grouped into a single routine PR per
# week so the queue stays reviewable, with security updates kept in their own
# group so an advisory fix is never hidden inside a large routine bump.
#
# `cooldown` deliberately lags fresh releases: this repo pins GitHub Actions
# by commit SHA, and a week is long enough for a yanked crate or a pulled
# action release to surface before it lands in a PR here.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-actions:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-actions:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: cargo
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      # The oxc_* crates are released in lockstep and their minor releases
      # carry breaking API changes; keeping them in one PR means the
      # extractor and resolver are updated together or not at all.
      oxc:

from pathlib import Path
import re
p=Path(".github/workflows/ci.yml"); s=p.read_text()

# 1. workflow-level default-deny, mirroring release.yml
old_conc = "# Cancel in-progress runs for the same branch/PR.\nconcurrency:"
new_conc = ("# Least privilege at workflow scope; each job opts into exactly what it needs.\n"
            "permissions: {}\n\n"
            "# Cancel in-progress runs for the same branch/PR.\nconcurrency:")
assert old_conc in s
s = s.replace(old_conc, new_conc, 1)

# 2. every job reads the repo and nothing else
s = re.sub(r"(?m)^    runs-on:", "    permissions:\n      contents: read\n    runs-on:", s)

# 3. checkout must not leave the token in .git/config for later steps
CO = "actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1"
s = s.replace(f"      - uses: {CO}\n        with:\n          fetch-depth: 0\n",
              f"      - uses: {CO}\n        with:\n          fetch-depth: 0\n          persist-credentials: false\n")
s = re.sub(rf"      - uses: {re.escape(CO)}\n(?!        with:)",
           f"      - uses: {CO}\n        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n", s)
p.write_text(s)
PY

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain

zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and

pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    typos
    cargo deny check
"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
s = s.replace(
    "# Simulate full CI locally (lint → test → deny → typos → doc-check → machete → ts tests)\nci: lint test deny typos doc-check machete test-ts",
    "# Simulate full CI locally (lint → test → deny → typos → zizmor → doc-check → machete → ts tests)\nci: lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete test-ts",
)
p.write_text(s)

# --- moon hooks call the recipe ---
p = Path(".moon/workspace.yml"); s = p.read_text()
old = """    pre-commit:

      - "just pre-commit\""""

content.text:
Everything below is verified green: `cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (537 tests)/doc/deny/machete`, `typos`, `zizmor`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, vite-plugin build + 33 tests.

**moon was the big one.** `.prototools` pinned moon 2.3.3, but `.moon/toolchain.yml` is the *moon 1.x* filename — v2 renamed it to `toolchains.yml`. moon has been silently ignoring that file, so every version in it (including `pnpm: "10"`, contradicting `.prototools`' `~11`) was dead config. Renamed and rewritten in v2 shape: each toolchain now inherits its version from `.prototools` via `versionFromPrototools`, with `rust.syncToolchainConfig: false` so moon can't write a competing `rust-toolchain.toml`. `.moon/workspace.yml` needed no changes — `vcs.client` is still valid in v2.

**Toolchain.** Rust 1.96.0 → 1.98.1 (current stable) in `.prototools` and CI's `RUST_VERSION`. 1.98's clippy flagged two real `question_mark` sites in `resolver/template.rs`, now fixed. moon 2.3.3 → **2.4.5, not 2.5.5**: 2.5.x requires proto ≥ 0.60.0 and yours is 0.57.4, which fails hard on the pnpm plugin. `proto upgrade` first, then 2.5.5 is available.

**Actions.** All pinned by commit SHA with version comments (callisto's policy), and bumped: checkout v4→v7.0.1, upload-artifact v4→v7.0.1, download-artifact v4→v8.0.1, codecov v5→v7.1.1, cargo-deny-action v2→v2.1.1, setup-toolchain v0→v0.6.4, orin-dx/actions v1.1→SHA. The `taiki-e/install-action@<tool>` shorthands became pinned refs with a `tool:` input (coverage's two steps merged into one).

**zizmor** found 30 issues, now zero. `ci.yml` had no `permissions:` anywhere (11 findings) and 10 checkouts leaving the token in `.git/config`. Added workflow-level `permissions: {}`, `contents: read` per job, and `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout. The one remaining finding — the deliberate lockfile-free install in the transitive-dep test — carries an inline ignore with its reason. Wired in as a `just zizmor` recipe plus an unconditional CI job pinned to zizmor 1.29.0 (the version I verified against).

**Dependabot** added: github-actions, cargo, and npm, weekly, 7-day cooldown, routine and security updates in separate groups. The `oxc_*` crates get their own group — they release in lockstep and break APIs in minors, so they must move together.

**Cargo.** `cargo update` refreshed the lockfile. Removed 8 dead `[workspace.dependencies]` entries (`oxc_module_lexer`, `indexmap`, `dirs`, `thiserror`, `anyhow`, `lsp-types`, `clap_mangen`, `tracing-indicatif`) — leftovers from the unused-deps changeset, still declared but referenced by no crate. Bumped the four out-of-caret-range ones: compact_str 0.9→0.10, criterion 0.7→0.8, rstest 0.25→0.27, trycmd 0.15→1.2. `deny.toml`'s 8 `skip` entries are gone — cargo-deny reported every one as unnecessary, because the duplicate oxc crate family came in through `oxc_module_lexer`; dropped the stale `MPL-2.0` allow with it (`option-ext` is no longer in the graph).

**npm.** In-range updates across the workspace, `@types/node` ^22→^26 (it was four majors behind the pinned Node 26), and vite ^7→^8 + vitest ^3→^5 — the plugin already advertised `vite: ^7 || ^8` as a peer but only tested against 7. Tests pass on 8.

**Snapshots needed a fix before dependabot lands.** Snapshot `fileName`s embed the pnpm store path, which contains the exact version: `.pnpm/@types+react@19.2.17/...`. The `@types/react` bump alone broke all 7 fixtures. Every weekly npm PR would have done the same, burying real extraction changes in version churn. Added a `[VERSION]` redaction (splitting at the first `@` after index 0, so scoped names and peer suffixes both work) with unit tests covering scoped, peer-suffixed, repeated, absent, and versionless segments. Snapshots regenerated: the only non-version diff is `mantine.snap`'s literal-union quoting, which was already modified in your working tree before this session.

**justfile:** added `zizmor` (wired into `just ci`) and a `pre-commit` recipe; `.moon/workspace.yml`'s hook now calls it instead of repeating the four commands. Run `moon sync vcs-hooks` to regenerate the hook.

Deliberately not done:

- **oxc 0.135 → 0.151.** Attempted and reverted — 15 compile errors in the core extractor, not a maintenance bump: `Class.super_class` and `super_type_arguments` gone, `ExportNamedDeclaration.declaration`/`.source` gone, `TSModuleDeclaration` and `TSModuleDeclarationName` removed from the AST and the `Visit` trait, `ParserReturn.errors` gone, `TSInterfaceHeritage.expression` gone. That touches ambient-module, export, and class-heritage handling with snapshot review required. Its own change.
- **typescript 5.9 → 7.0** (the Go port), **react-docgen 7 → 8** (it's the accuracy-comparison baseline — bumping moves the thing we measure against), **chalk 5 → 6**, **pnpm 11 → 12** (lockfile format risk).
- No changeset: everything here is internal tooling with no consumer-visible behavior change.
With all of these changes should we make a PR? Then make a PR to move oxc?

Before I push anything — I dug into PR #3 and found it's red, for two causes that matter here.

All six TypeScript/Install/Format jobs fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`: commit `ef8cec9` changed `packages/cli/package.json` without regenerating `pnpm-lock.yaml`. My dependency work already fixes that — `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes now.

Test and Coverage fail separately: `crates/cli`'s config tests spawn `node --import=tsx/esm` against a real `docgen.config.ts`, and `tsx` is a devDependency of `apps/validate` that isn't hoisted to the root, so the Rust-only jobs have no `node_modules`. I just added moon + `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` to the `test` and `coverage` jobs. zizmor still clean.

So PR #3 can't merge without my changes, which makes "stack a second PR on it" a PR against a red base.

One thing I won't touch without you saying so: your working tree has ~334 lines of unrelated in-progress work — the `LiteralUnion` quoting fix in `extractor/alias.rs`, plus `watch.rs`, `pipeline/mod.rs`, `extract.rs`, and the type-checker ADRs. That's also the real source of `mantine.snap`'s `"\"xs\"" → "xs"` diff, not my redaction. If I commit, I'll stage only my files and rewrite `mantine.snap` to carry the version redaction alone, then restore your version to the working tree.

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(core): store literal-union alias members bare instead of pre-quoted

`ts_type_to_collected` built LiteralUnion members with `to_raw_string()`, which
wraps a string literal in quotes. Every serializer quotes LiteralUnion members
itself, so a `type Size = "sm" | "md"` alias rendered as `""sm"" | ""md""`, and
a template literal over it expanded to `compact-"sm"`.

Members are now the bare values. Two union shapes needed deciding along the
way: `undefined` is dropped, matching what `resolve_union` already does --
optionality belongs in `required` -- while `null` is a real value a string-only
LiteralUnion cannot hold, so it keeps the alias a plain Union.

CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION goes to 4. The cache key is a content hash, so it cannot
notice that the extractor now produces different SourceData for byte-identical
input; without the bump a warm cache would serve pre-quoted members forever.

fix(release): adopt callisto 0.8's release-PR and durable-execute split

callisto 0.8 removed the action's `publish` input. callisto-action now only
creates or updates the release PR; publication runs from the merged release
commit under the repository's own workflow. The old single-step
`publish: "true"` job would have silently published nothing.

release.yml becomes that durable workflow: identify a merged, GitHub-verified
callisto/version-packages commit, derive an intent from its actual delta with
`callisto release plan --from-release-commit`, hand it between jobs as a
same-run artifact with a SHA-256 sidecar, then `callisto release execute`
behind a `release` environment that is the only place registry credentials
exist. Both callisto actions are pinned to callisto@0.8.0's commit, and
setup-callisto is invoked explicitly so the CLI version is pinned here rather
than inherited from the action's default.

callisto.toml carried a `publish-to = "cratesIo"` that the parser rejects --
the value is `crates-io` -- so the whole config failed to load and none of the
per-package overrides were ever applied. Fixed, and the fixed-group members are
now ecosystem-qualified.

The private root package.json was named `oxc-react-docgen`, colliding with the
CLI crate: callisto resolves bare names through an identity index that errors on
ambiguity rather than guessing, so every `oxc-react-docgen: patch` changeset was
unresolvable. Renamed to `oxc-react-docgen-workspace`; it is referenced nowhere
else and pnpm keys importers by path.

No `[release]` section: 0.8 validates `artifact-targets` against callisto's own
hardcoded asset-name table, so no other workspace can declare one. The plan job
asserts the derived intent carries no artifact slots.

cat > .changeset/literal-union-bare-members.md <<'MD'
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

String-literal union aliases now report bare member values. A `type Size = "sm" | "md"` alias previously came back with each member already quoted, so serialized output showed `""sm"" | ""md""` and a template literal over the alias expanded to `compact-"sm"`. `undefined` members are dropped (optionality is reported through `required`); a `null` member keeps the alias a plain union, since a string-only literal union can't represent it.

The DTS cache schema version moved to 4 — its key is a content hash and can't detect that the extractor now produces different data for identical input, so existing cache files are discarded rather than served stale.
MD
cat > .changeset/ambient-dts-types-not-components.md <<'MD'
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

Ambient `.d.ts` files are merged for their types only, never their components. `@types/react` declares `class PureComponent<P, S, SS> extends Component<P, S, SS>`, which matched the class-component detector — full HTML-attribute mode emitted `PureComponent` as a 0-prop component alongside a `Cannot resolve type 'P'` diagnostic. Both are gone, from batch extraction and from the watch session's first revision.
MD

---

`--format rdt` omits a `children` prop that has no description, matching react-docgen-typescript's default `skipChildrenPropWithoutDoc`. A documented `children` is still emitted, and `--format canonical` is unchanged.
